claims.statement: Reverting to allocation rule v17 did not clear the stuck 186 orders; they remain held
claims.corroboration: Revert outcome (tier-1, Observability) explicitly states held orders unchanged at 186 after v17 restoration

claims.statement: After reverting to v17, newly allocated orders routed to east node are also held; the issue is not order-specific but location-specific (east node)
claims.corroboration: Revert outcome (tier-1, Observability) states new east-node allocations are still held after v17 restoration
claims.limitation: Does not identify whether issue is dock capacity, carrier, or inventory at east node

claims.statement: ROOT1 (allocation rule v18 is root cause) is disproven by revert outcome: orders remain stuck after reverting to v17, and new v17-allocated east-node orders are also stuck
claims.corroboration: Revert mitigation (tier-1, Observability) shows v18 is not the root cause; the issue persists after reverting to v17; new allocations to east node also exhibit the same hold behavior
claims.limitation: None; causality is clear from failure of revert mitigation

claims.statement: Carrier pickup integration at east node is unable to execute or accept orders; either carrier feed is lagging only for east-node lanes, or carrier explicitly blocks east-node pickups
claims.corroboration: All stuck orders are east-node routed regardless of allocation rule (v17 or v18); other nodes are normal (m8_e02); observability gap (m8_e09) prevents carrier confirmation visibility
claims.limitation: Requires carrier ops confirmation; could also be dock capacity or inventory shortage at east node

claims.statement: East node dock or staging capacity is saturated; 186 orders + subsequent allocations cannot proceed because physical dock space is unavailable
claims.corroboration: Large cohort of 186 orders at east node; new allocations also held at east node; other nodes normal; timing suggests sustained capacity constraint rather than transient
claims.limitation: Requires real-time dock capacity audit to confirm

contradictions.claim_b: C9: reverting v18 did not clear orders
contradictions.description: If v18 were the root cause, reverting it should clear the stuck orders. The fact that they remain stuck and new v17 orders are also stuck disproves ROOT1
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: None; contradiction is resolved by m8_r_revert outcome

resolutions.outcome: ROOT1 disproven; root cause is not allocation rule change but rather an east-node specific issue (carrier, dock, or inventory)
resolutions.rationale: Revert mitigation is a definitive test: if v18 were the cause, reverting must clear orders. It did not. Therefore v18 is not the root cause. The pattern shows all east-node allocations are stuck regardless of rule version

capability_gaps.capability: Real-time east node dock capacity and utilization
capability_gaps.reason: Critical to determine if dock is at or over capacity, blocking carrier pickup execution

capability_gaps.capability: Carrier ops confirmation: did carrier receive and attempt execution of east-node pickup requests for both original and re-allocated orders?
capability_gaps.reason: Would discriminate carrier-side block from dock/inventory issues

next_action.rationale: ROOT1 is now disproven: reverting v18 to v17 did not clear orders, and new v17-allocated east-node orders are also held. This rules out allocation rule change as root cause. The pattern is location-specific: ALL east-node allocations are stuck regardless of rule version. This narrows root cause to east node itself: either (a) dock capacity exhausted, preventing carrier pickup staging, (b) carrier feed issue specific to east-node lanes, or (c) inventory shortage at east node. Checking dock capacity first will quickly determine if the dock is the blocker; if capacity is available, then carrier or inventory is the issue
next_action.expected_information_gain: Determine whether east node dock is at/over capacity (immediate blocker) or if capacity is available (points to carrier or inventory issue)
